cases.reason: System A and System B represent different QU information states because System A uses a single shared carrier while System B uses two distinct carriers with an equality constraint. QU preserves this distinction as it is structurally load-bearing. Natural identity does not automatically follow from value equality.

NEI prohibits silently averaging over QU realizations to produce a single scalar weight when the weight varies and no probability distribution is qualified. Realization-conditioned evidence must be preserved instead.
An exact domain theorem forces coidentity in every model, yielding a SAME status. Finite probabilistic evidence does not cause this exact status but can coexist with it in the record.
DP cannot upgrade structural correspondence to natural identity without NEI authority. Since required identity model/closure authority is absent, the identity query is incomplete.

The observations measure different semantic quantities (citations vs. artifacts), so they do not conflict. Qualification does not fail, and the discrepancy exposes an open structural lead for a hidden distinction.
A real decoder error can be repaired once the defect owner is established. However, the repair does not close the open structural lead regarding the derivable relation.
Scoped equivalence under view C is valid but does not imply global identity. Since admissible models include both coidentity and separation, the NEI status is UNKNOWN.
A partial common core is valid, but because R5 is outside the core and load-bearing, a full global isomorphism cannot be claimed, and R5 must remain a residual.
Naive summing of log Bayes factors is prohibited because the evidence records are correlated (shared causal lineage) and no conditional-independence authority exists. Dependence must be preserved.
QU refinement Q2 narrows the realization family, excluding SAME-compatible models and resulting in a DISTINCT status. Historical Q1 UNKNOWN records are not rewritten.
Different application class labels do not imply DISTINCT unless a domain law makes the classification identity-separating.
Restricting the QU state solely to force a desired identity result is circular and inadmissible under both QU and NEI specifications.
Qualification may complete when all obligations are met, even if a discovery lead remains open, as long as it does not undermine the completeness claim.
When a mismatch is proved to be a local implementation error and structural explanations are falsified, DP may close the lead without manufacturing an equivalence.

self_audit.notes: The analysis was performed using only the provided specifications for Core 0.18, QU 0.1, NEI 0.4, and DP 0.5/0.6. All cases were evaluated compositionally and independently.
